2 Thessalonians — Book introduction (Modern English candidate)

Paul wrote this second letter to the Thessalonians soon after the first.

He had learned that some believers had understood his earlier letter as predicting that Christ's return and the day of judgment would occur during their own lifetime.

Some responded by neglecting their ordinary earthly responsibilities.

Paul wrote again to correct this misunderstanding, which was also interfering with the spread of the gospel.

His earlier teaching agreed with the prophets of the Old Testament.

There were still purposes in God's eternal counsel to be fulfilled before the Lord's day.

He had spoken of Christ's return as near because its certainty makes it ever relevant, not because its date had been revealed.

This teaching led Paul to foretell remarkable events in the later history of the Christian church, demonstrating the prophetic gift with which God had equipped him.

Original chapter outlineOriginal outlineVersesThe apostle blesses God for the growing state of the love and patience of the Thessalonians.1–4And encourages them to persevere under all their sufferings for Christ, considering his coming at the great day of account.5–12
Faith, love and patience grow under affliction (verses 1–4)

Where saving grace is genuine, it will also grow.

The path of the righteous is like light growing brighter and brighter until the perfect day.

When we observe this growth, all the glory belongs to God.

As faith becomes stronger, love should also increase, because faith works through love.

The Thessalonians' patience and faith deserved to be held up as an example to other Christians.

Their sufferings were not proof that God's grace had failed.

Rather, trials permitted by Providence and persecution inflicted by people increased the exercise of their faith and patience, enabling them to remain firm through trouble.

Christ's return brings justice, rest and glory (verses 5–10)

If our religion is worth anything, it is worth everything.

People who cannot bring themselves to suffer for it either lack genuine religion or have not learned how precious it is.

Yet suffering does not earn heaven, any more than good works earn it.

Patient endurance can prepare us to enjoy the promised joy, but it does not purchase that joy.

One of the clearest signs of a person moving toward destruction is a spirit of persecution and hostility toward God's people.

The Lord will bring judgment upon those who trouble his servants.

There remains a rest for God's people, free from sin and sorrow.

God's righteousness guarantees that good and evil will receive their final judgment.

This assurance should terrify hardened sinners and sustain believers.

Faith that looks toward judgment can begin to understand some of Providence's difficult purposes, which otherwise appear confused and inexplicable to unbelievers.

Jesus will appear from heaven in the glory and power of the heavenly world.

His light will expose and his power will consume those who are like worthless chaff.

This appearing will be dreadful for people who refuse to know God—especially those who reject his revealed gospel or profess to believe it while refusing obedience.

The truth of the gospel is given to us so that we may obey its commands.

Sinners may be spared for a long time, but their final punishment will certainly come.

They have chosen to do sin's work and will receive sin's wages.

In this life God often judges sinners through created instruments.

At the final day, destruction will come from the Almighty himself.

How dreadful to meet the full power of his anger!

But that day will be joyful for believers who receive and obey Christ's gospel.

Jesus Christ will be admired and glorified by his saints and within his saints.

His grace and power will be displayed in everything he has purchased, accomplished and bestowed upon them.

How magnificent the glory he will give his people!

Yet how much more splendid is the Giver of that glory.

God's justice in judging wicked people will be acknowledged.

But the glory of his mercy in saving believers will be an even greater cause of wonder and worship.

Even angels will marvel.

The most ordinary believer will receive happiness beyond the widest human imagination, for Christ will be glorified in all those who believe, without exception.

Pray for God to complete the work of faith (verses 11 and 12)

Faith in Christ's coming should make us pray more, both for ourselves and for other people.

Every good quality in a believer springs from God's gracious good pleasure.

That is why it is called grace.

God has many merciful purposes for his people.

Paul prayed that he would complete their work of faith through divine power, so that other acts of obedience would also grow.

God's power not only begins faith but continues and sustains it.

This is the purpose of the grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ, revealed to and at work within believers.
classic_reading:
[2Thess.1.1-2Thess.1.4]
2 Thessalonians
The second epistle to the Thessalonians was written soon after the first. The apostle was told that, from some expressions in his first letter, many expected the second coming of Christ was at hand, and that the day of judgment would arrive in their time. Some of these neglected their worldly duties. St. Paul wrote again to correct their error, which hindered the spread of the gospel. He had written agreeably to the words of the prophets of the Old Testament; and he tells them there were many counsels of the Most High yet to be fulfilled, before that day of the Lord should come, though, because it is sure, he had spoken of it as near. The subject led to a remarkable foretelling, of some of the future events which were to take place in the after-ages of the Christian church, and which show the prophetic spirit the apostle possessed.
Chapter 1
Chapter Outline
The apostle blesses God for the growing state of the love and patience of the Thessalonians. | (1-4) |
And encourages them to persevere under all their sufferings for Christ, considering his coming at the great day of account. | (5-12) |
Verses 1-4
Where there is the truth of grace, there will be an increase of it. The path of the just is as the shining light, which shines more and more unto the perfect day. And where there is the increase of grace, God must have all the glory. Where faith grows, love will abound, for faith works by love. It shows faith and patience, such as may be proposed as a pattern for others, when trials from God, and persecutions from men, quicken the exercise of those graces; for the patience and faith of which the apostle gloried, bore them up, and enabled them to endure all their tribulations.
[2Thess.1.5-2Thess.1.10]
Verses 5-10
Religion, if worth anything, is worth every thing; and those have no religion, or none worth having, or know not how to value it, cannot find their hearts to suffer for it. We cannot by all our sufferings, any more than by our services, merit heaven; but by our patience under sufferings, we are prepared for the promised joy. Nothing more strongly marks a man for eternal ruin, than a spirit of persecution and enmity to the name and people of God. God will trouble those that trouble his people. And there is a rest for the people of God; a rest from sin and sorrow. The certainty of future recompence is proved by the righteousness of God. The thoughts of this should be terrible to wicked men, and support the righteous. Faith, looking to the great day, is enabled partly to understand the book of providence, which appears confused to unbelievers. The Lord Jesus will in that day appear from heaven. He will come in the glory and power of the upper world. His light will be piercing, and his power consuming, to all who in that day shall be found as chaff. This appearance will be terrible to those that know not God, especially to those who rebel against revelation, and obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. This is the great crime of multitudes, the gospel is revealed, and they will not believe it; or if they pretend to believe, they will not obey it. Believing the truths of the gospel, is in order to our obeying the precepts of the gospel. Though sinners may be long spared, they will be punished at last. They did sin's work, and must receive sin's wages. Here God punishes sinners by creatures as instruments; but then, it will be destruction from the Almighty; and who knows the power of his anger? It will be a joyful day to some, to the saints, to those who believe and obey the gospel. In that bright and blessed day, Christ Jesus will be glorified and admired by his saints. And Christ will be glorified and admired in them. His grace and power will be shown, when it shall appear what he has purchased for, and wrought in, and bestowed upon those who believe in him. Lord, if the glory put upon thy saints shall be thus admired, how much more shalt thou be admired, as the Bestower of that glory! The glory of thy justice in the damnation of the wicked will be admired, but not as the glory of thy mercy in the salvation of believers. How will this strike the adoring angels with holy admiration, and transport thy admiring saints with eternal rapture! The meanest believer shall enjoy more than the most enlarged heart can imagine while we are here; Christ will be admired in all those that believe, the meanest believer not excepted.
[2Thess.1.11-2Thess.1.12]
Verses 11-12
Believing thoughts and expectations of the second coming of Christ should lead us to pray to God more, for ourselves and others. If there is any good in us, it is owing to the good pleasure of his goodness, and therefore it is called grace. There are many purposes of grace and good-will in God toward his people, and the apostle prays that God would complete in them the work of faith with power. This is to their doing every other good work. The power of God not only begins, but carries on the work of faith. And this is the great end and design of the grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ, which is made known to us, and wrought in us.

There would first be a general apostasy from the faith, and a revealing of the antichristian man of sin.1–4His destruction, and that of those who obey him.5–12The security of the Thessalonians from apostacy; an exhortation to stedfastness, and prayer for them.13–17
Do not be deceived about the Lord's return (verses 1–4)

When errors arise among Christians, we should correct them.

Faithful servants should be especially careful to remedy mistakes that have grown from misunderstanding their own words or actions.

Our cunning adversary looks for opportunities to harm us.

Satan may encourage false teaching even through the misuse of Scripture's words.

We may be unsure about the time of Christ's return, but we have every reason to be sure that he will return.

Believers in every generation of the church, and the faithful before Christ's first coming, have trusted this promise.

All God's people will be gathered to Christ to live with him in happiness forever.

But wrongly assuming the time is already at hand creates a danger.

When the predicted date passes, the disappointed person may begin to doubt the event's certainty itself.

False doctrines resemble wind that makes water churn and ripple.

Our minds can be just as unstable.

It is enough to know that Jesus will return and gather his people.

Paul gave a reason the Thessalonians should not yet expect the final day: a great falling away would take place first, bringing the revelation of the man of sin, Antichrist.

People have debated at length who or what this figure is.

The man of sin not only commits wicked acts but promotes and commands others to sin.

He is called a son of destruction because his own ruin is certain, while he becomes the instrument through which many others are destroyed in body and soul.

The imagery of God's temple points to a usurper who claims God's authority within the Christian church and demands honors belonging to God alone.

Corrupt religion and false miracles (verses 5–12)

Something was restraining the full appearance of the man of sin.

Henry supposes that this restraint was the power of the Roman Empire, which Paul did not name explicitly at the time.

Corruption in doctrine and worship, followed by the usurpation of authority, entered gradually.

Thus the mystery of lawlessness advanced step by step.

Superstition and idolatry were promoted under the appearance of devotion.

Bigotry and persecution were justified through claims of zeal for God's glory.

The mystery of lawlessness had already begun during the apostles' lives, when some professed zeal for Christ but actually opposed him.

Paul announced the destruction of this antichristian condition.

God's pure word joined with God's Spirit exposes its deceit.

In the Lord's appointed time, it will be destroyed through the brightness of Christ's coming.

False signs, visions and miracles can be used to support deceptive doctrine.

Some may be fraudulent displays or claimed miracles intended to mislead people.

Those willingly deceived did not love the truth and therefore refused to believe it.

They found pleasure in false notions.

God leaves such people to themselves, and they consequently enter deeper sin, experience spiritual judgment here and face eternal punishment afterward.

Henry concludes that many of these prophecies had already been fulfilled and confirmed Scripture's truth.

As a seventeenth- and eighteenth-century Protestant commentator, he specifically identifies the papal system and the Roman Catholic Church with this antichristian pattern.

That identification is preserved as Henry's historical interpretation, not as an independently established fact or as a replacement of the biblical text.

He also insists that the Lord has not yet completely destroyed this evil through his appearing, and that further prophecies remain to be fulfilled before the end.

The elect persevere through faith and the Spirit's holiness (verses 13–15)

When many turn away from the faith, we can rejoice that God preserves a remnant chosen by grace.

We should also desire evidence that we belong to that remnant.

The perseverance of God's children rests upon his everlasting love, present from before the world's foundation.

Yet the promised end must never be separated from the appointed means.

Faith and holiness belong together, just as holiness and eternal happiness belong together.

God's outward call comes through the gospel.

That call becomes effective through the inward work of the Holy Spirit.

Believing God's truth brings the sinner to trust Christ, love him and obey his commands.

The Holy Spirit seals the gospel upon the heart.

Henry says we have no certain evidence of any apostolic teachings delivered outside the contents of Holy Scripture.

Therefore we should hold firmly to the apostolic doctrines preserved in Scripture and reject unsupported additions and vain traditions.

Christ himself gives enduring comfort (verses 16 and 17)

We may and should pray not only to God the Father through Jesus, but also directly to the Lord Jesus Christ, our Savior.

We pray in Christ's name to his Father, who has also become our Father through him.

The love of God in Jesus Christ is the fountain of everything good we now possess or hope to receive.

Believers have strong reason to receive lasting consolation, because grace gives them a secure hope.

The free grace and mercy of God—not personal worth or merit—are the foundation of that hope.

The more joy we take in God's word, deeds and ways, the more likely we are to persevere in them.

When we waver in faith, hesitate in our duties or continue in uncertainty and distrust, it is no surprise that we fail to experience the joys of Christian faith.
classic_reading:
[2Thess.2.1-2Thess.2.4]
Chapter 2
Chapter Outline
Cautions against the error that the time of Christ's coming was just at hand. There would first be a general apostasy from the faith, and a revealing of the antichristian man of sin.
(1-4)
His destruction, and that of those who obey him.
(5-12)
The security of the Thessalonians from apostacy; an exhortation to stedfastness, and prayer for them.
(13-17)
Verses 1-4
If errors arise among Christians, we should set them right; and good men will be careful to suppress errors which rise from mistaking their words and actions. We have a cunning adversary, who watches to do mischief, and will promote errors, even by the words of Scripture. Whatever uncertainty we are in, or whatever mistakes may arise about the time of Christ's coming, that coming itself is certain. This has been the faith and hope of all Christians, in all ages of the church; it was the faith and hope of the Old Testament saints. All believers shall be gathered together to Christ, to be with him, and to be happy in his presence for ever. We should firmly believe the second coming of Christ; but there was danger lest the Thessalonians, being mistaken as to the time, should question the truth or certainty of the thing itself. False doctrines are like the winds that toss the water to and fro; and they unsettle the minds of men, which are as unstable as water. It is enough for us to know that our Lord will come, and will gather all his saints unto him. A reason why they should not expect the coming of Christ, as at hand, is given. There would be a general falling away first, such as would occasion the rise of antichrist, that man of sin. There have been great disputes who or what is intended by this man of sin and son of perdition. The man of sin not only practises wickedness, but also promotes and commands sin and wickedness in others; and is the son of perdition, because he is devoted to certain destruction, and is the instrument to destroy many others, both in soul and body. As God was in the temple of old, and worshipped there, and is in and with his church now; so the antichrist here mentioned, is a usurper of God's authority in the Christian church, who claims Divine honours.
[2Thess.2.5-2Thess.2.12]
Verses 5-12
Something hindered or withheld the man of sin. It is supposed to be the power of the Roman empire, which the apostle did not mention more plainly at that time. Corruption of doctrine and worship came in by degrees, and the usurping of power was gradual; thus the mystery of iniquity prevailed. Superstition and idolatry were advanced by pretended devotion, and bigotry and persecution were promoted by pretended zeal for God and his glory. This mystery of iniquity was even then begun; while the apostles were yet living, persons pretended zeal for Christ, but really opposed him. The fall or ruin of the antichristian state is declared. The pure word of God, with the Spirit of God, will discover this mystery of iniquity, and in due time it shall be destroyed by the brightness of Christ's coming. Signs and wonders, visions and miracles, are pretended; but they are false signs to support false doctrines; and lying wonders, or only pretended miracles, to cheat the people; and the diabolical deceits with which the antichristian state has been supported, are notorious. The persons are described, who are his willing subjects. Their sin is this; They did not love the truth, and therefore did not believe it; and they were pleased with false notions. God leaves them to themselves, then sin will follow of course, and spiritual judgments here, and eternal punishments hereafter. These prophecies have, in a great measure, come to pass, and confirm the truth of the Scriptures. This passage exactly agrees with the system of popery, as it prevails in the Romish church, and under the Romish popes. But though the son of perdition has been revealed, though he has opposed and exalted himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; and has spoken and acted as if he were a god upon earth, and has proclaimed his insolent pride, and supported his delusions, by lying miracles and all kinds of frauds; still the Lord has not yet fully destroyed him with the brightness of his coming; that and other prophecies remain to be fulfilled before the end shall come.
[2Thess.2.13-2Thess.2.15]
Verses 13-15
When we hear of the apostacy of many, it is a great comfort and joy, that there is a remnant according to the election of grace, which does and shall persevere; especially we should rejoice, if we have reason to hope that we are of that number. The preservation of the saints, is because God loved them with an everlasting love, from the beginning of the world. The end and the means must not be separated. Faith and holiness must be joined together as well as holiness and happiness. The outward call of God is by the gospel; and this is rendered effectual by the inward working of the Spirit. The belief of the truth brings the sinner to rely on Christ, and so to love and obey him; it is sealed by the Holy Spirit upon his heart. We have no certain proof of any thing having been delivered by the apostles, more than what we find contained in the Holy Scriptures. Let us then stand fast in the doctrines taught by the apostles, and reject all additions, and vain traditions.
[2Thess.2.16-2Thess.2.17]
Verses 16-17
We may and should direct our prayers, not only to God the Father, through our Lord Jesus Christ, but also to our Lord Jesus Christ himself. And we should pray in his name unto God, not only as his Father, but as our Father in and through him. The love of God in Christ Jesus, is the spring and fountain of all the good we have or hope for. There is good reason for strong consolations, because the saints have good hope through grace. The free grace and mercy of God are what they hope for, and what their hopes are founded on, and not any worth or merit of their own. The more pleasure we take in the word, and works, and ways of God, the more likely we shall be to persevere therein. But, if we are wavering in faith, and of a doubtful mind, halting and faltering in our duty, no wonder that we are strangers to the joys of religion.

Original chapter outlineOriginal outlineVersesThe apostle expresses confidence in the Thessalonians, and prays for them.1–5He charges them to withdraw from disorderly walkers, particularly from the lazy and busybodies.6–15And concludes with a prayer for them, and a greeting.16–18
Pray for faithful gospel work and for one another (verses 1–5)

Christians who live far apart can still meet at the throne of grace.

Even when people can offer one another no other practical help, they may give and receive genuine, valuable service through prayer.

Opponents of gospel preaching and persecutors of faithful ministers act unreasonably and wickedly.

Many do not believe the gospel. We should not be surprised when such people become restless and malicious toward those who proclaim it.

Sin itself is the greatest evil, but there are other dangers from which we need God's protection.

His gracious promises encourage us to trust him.

When God has given his promise, its fulfillment is certain.

Paul was confident about the Thessalonians, but that confidence was founded upon his confidence in God, not on human reliability.

He prayed for spiritual blessings.

We are sinful and miserable because we so often set our affections upon the wrong things.

There is no genuine love of God without faith in Jesus Christ.

If through God's special grace we possess this saving faith, we should earnestly ask for grace to obey the Lord without reservation, loving God and patiently enduring for Christ's sake.

Do honest work, correct the disorderly and never tire of doing good (verses 6–15)

Those who have received Christ's gospel must live in ways appropriate to it.

People who were able to work but refused to work should not be supported in their deliberate idleness.

Christianity does not endorse laziness.

Resources consumed by those unwilling to work are then unavailable to encourage diligent people or support the sick and afflicted.

Being faithful in our ordinary employment is also a duty of our Christian calling.

Some people wanted support while doing no work.

They also became meddlesome and self-important, interfering with other people's affairs.

They caused considerable harm.

Using religion as a disguise for idleness or any other sin is a serious corruption of Christianity.

A servant waiting properly for the return of the Master should be doing the work the Master commanded.

An idle mind is easily occupied by Satan and our own sinful desires.

The human mind is always active. If it is not doing good, it will often turn toward evil.

It is a rare and excellent combination to be energetic in one's own work and quiet about other people's affairs.

Those who refused to work peacefully were to be corrected.

Believers could withdraw familiar fellowship from them when necessary.

Yet the aim remained their good, and correction should take the form of loving admonition, not hatred.

God will be with those who continue in his ways.

Do not grow tired of doing good.

Continue faithfully until your task is finished.

The time for complete rest will come in heaven.

Pray for peace and Christ's grace (verses 16–18)

Paul prayed for the Thessalonians, and we should seek the same blessings for ourselves and our friends.

He especially desired peace with God.

He prayed that they would enjoy that peace always and in every circumstance, using all the means of grace God provides.

We can wish nothing better for those we love than God's gracious presence.

If the Lord is with us, our location and the absence of other people cannot destroy our happiness.

Through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ we hope to enjoy peace with God and his presence.

His grace supplies everything necessary for true safety and happiness.

However much grace we ask God to give other people, there will always be enough for us too.
classic_reading:
[2Thess.3.1-2Thess.3.5]
Chapter 3
Chapter Outline
The apostle expresses confidence in the Thessalonians, and prays for them. | (1-5) |
He charges them to withdraw from disorderly walkers, particularly from the lazy and busybodies. | (6-15) |
And concludes with a prayer for them, and a greeting. | (16-18) |
Verses 1-5
Those who are far apart still may meet together at the throne of grace; and those not able to do or receive any other kindness, may in this way do and receive real and very great kindness. Enemies to the preaching of the gospel, and persecutors of its faithful preachers, are unreasonable and wicked men. Many do not believe the gospel; and no wonder if such are restless and show malice in their endeavours to oppose it. The evil of sin is the greatest evil, but there are other evils we need to be preserved from, and we have encouragement to depend upon the grace of God. When once the promise is made, the performance is sure and certain. The apostle had confidence in them, but that was founded upon his confidence in God; for there is otherwise no confidence in man. He prays for them for spiritual blessings. It is our sin and our misery, that we place our affections upon wrong objects. There is not true love of God, without faith in Jesus Christ. If, by the special grace of God, we have that faith which multitudes have not, we should earnestly pray that we may be enabled, without reserve, to obey his commands, and that we may be enabled, without reserve, to the love of God, and the patience of Christ.
[2Thess.3.6-2Thess.3.15]
Verses 6-15
Those who have received the gospel, are to live according to the gospel. Such as could work, and would not, were not to be maintained in idleness. Christianity is not to countenance slothfulness, which would consume what is meant to encourage the industrious, and to support the sick and afflicted. Industry in our callings as men, is a duty required by our calling as Christians. But some expected to be maintained in idleness, and indulged a curious and conceited temper. They meddled with the concerns of others, and did much harm. It is a great error and abuse of religion, to make it a cloak for idleness or any other sin. The servant who waits for the coming of his Lord aright, must be working as his Lord has commanded. If we are idle, the devil and a corrupt heart will soon find us somewhat to do. The mind of man is a busy thing; if it is not employed in doing good, it will be doing evil. It is an excellent, but rare union, to be active in our own business, yet quiet as to other people's. If any refused to labour with quietness, they were to note him with censure, and to separate from his company, yet they were to seek his good by loving admonitions. The Lords is with you while you are with him. Hold on your way, and hold on to the end. We must never give over, or tire in our work. It will be time enough to rest when we come to heaven.
[2Thess.3.16-2Thess.3.18]
Verses 16-18
The apostle prays for the Thessalonians. And let us desire the same blessings for ourselves and our friends. Peace with God. This peace is desired for them always, or in every thing. Peace by all means; in every way; that, as they enjoyed the means of grace, they might use all methods to secure peace. We need nothing more to make us safe and happy, nor can we desire any thing better for ourselves and our friends, than to have God's gracious presence with us and them. No matter where we are, if God be with us; nor who is absent, if God be present. It is through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that we hope to have peace with God, and to enjoy the presence of God. This grace is all in all to make us happy; though we wish ever so much to others, there remains enough for ourselves.
